questions.q: Whenever $\frac{-3x^3 + 12x}{x^3 - x^2 - 6x}$ is defined, it is equivalent to:
questions.explain: First, factor both the numerator and the denominator. The numerator is $-3x^3 + 12x = -3x(x^2 - 4) = -3x(x - 2)(x + 2)$. The denominator is $x^3 - x^2 - 6x = x(x^2 - x - 6) = x(x - 3)(x + 2)$. The expression becomes $\frac{-3x(x - 2)(x + 2)}{x(x - 3)(x + 2)}$. Cancel out the common terms, $x$ and $(x + 2)$, which gives $\frac{-3(x - 2)}{x - 3}$. Distribute the $-3$ in the numerator to get $\frac{-3x + 6}{x - 3}$, which can be rewritten as $\frac{6 - 3x}{x - 3}$.
